headline: Indonesian Immigration Denies Claims Of 90 Million Passport Data Leak
seoTitle: Indonesian Immigration Denies Passport Data Leak
metaDescription: The Directorate General of Immigration in Indonesia has officially refuted reports concerning a security breach of 90 million passport records.
aiSummaryBullets: Director General of Immigration Hendarsam Marantoko denied any cyberattack or leakage involving 90 million Indonesian passport data.
Immigration officials stated that the allegations of a data breach appear intended to diminish public trust in the institution.
The government has announced plans to report the individuals spreading these claims to the police for further investigation.
aiContextParagraph: The Directorate General of Immigration under the Indonesian Ministry of Immigration and Correctional Affairs has addressed widespread reports regarding an alleged security breach of 90 million passport records. Director General of Immigration Hendarsam Marantoko firmly refuted these claims, asserting that no cyberattacks had occurred and no personal data had been compromised. Officials suggested that the rumors might be a deliberate attempt to undermine public confidence in national immigration systems. In response to the misinformation, authorities indicated they would involve law enforcement to investigate those responsible for spreading the reports. While addressing these security concerns, the institution concurrently announced service updates, including the 'Paspor Ringkas' initiative and enhancements to autogate systems at airports, aimed at streamlining passport applications and processing for citizens using electronic national identity cards.
whyItIsViral: The story is trending due to coverage by five independent media outlets and a high velocity of news reporting regarding potential national security risks.
